summary: The reader has finished a standard undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics (induction, counting, modular arithmetic, primes, gcd, permutations, basic graphs), algorithms (asymptotic notation, divide and conquer, recurrences, sorting including radix sort, the idea of the FFT and Karatsuba multiplication at survey level), calculus and basic real analysis (limits, logarithms, exponentials, floors and ceilings, inequalities), introductory linear algebra and probability, and the basics of Turing machines and complexity. They have not studied abstract algebra beyond arithmetic mod n, coding theory, or number-theoretic transforms in depth, and have not met the multitape fast-multiplication literature (Schönhage–Strassen, Fürer, Harvey–van der Hoeven), Gaussian resampling, or Nussbaumer polynomial transforms.

known.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: Θ, Ω and o describe tight, lower and strictly smaller growth rates of functions of n, and limits and liminf of ratios such as T(n)/(n lg n) are the usual way to compare them.

known.name: Logarithms, exponentials, floors and ceilings
known.gloss: The binary logarithm lg n, powers 2^k, the floor and ceiling functions, and manipulation of expressions such as (lg n)^(1-κ) and ⌈log₂ n⌉ for bit lengths.

known.name: Binary and radix-b representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is a sum of digits times powers of a radix, so an n-bit string denotes an integer below 2^n and can be regrouped into digits of any larger radix such as 2^b.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and Karatsuba
known.gloss: Quadratic-time digit-by-digit multiplication, used here for small inputs, and the existence of faster divide-and-conquer multiplication such as Karatsuba's O(n^1.585) method.

known.name: Divisibility, primes and gcd
known.gloss: Divisibility, prime numbers, greatest common divisors and coprimality, and finding small primes by trial division.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and residue classes
known.gloss: Arithmetic on remainders modulo a positive integer, including cyclic shifts of indices mod Q, division with remainder q = ⌊a/b⌋ and r = a − bq, and multiplicative inverses of units mod n.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: The complex numbers satisfying z^n = 1 are e^{2πik/n}; a primitive one generates them all, and sums of their powers vanish except in the trivial case.

known.name: Recurrences and geometric series
known.gloss: Bounding the cost of a recursive procedure by unrolling a recurrence of the form T(n) ≤ a T(n/b) + f(n) and summing a geometric series.

known.name: Induction and elementary proof technique
known.gloss: Proving statements about all n by induction, contradiction or counting arguments.

known.name: Elementary counting and the union bound
known.gloss: Counting subsets and tuples, binomial coefficients, and bounding the size of a union of bad sets by the sum of their sizes.

known.name: Sorting and radix sort
known.gloss: Sorting records by integer keys, including the idea of a stable sort and radix sort as repeated stable passes on digits.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite index set to itself, applied to rearrange array entries and composed or inverted.

known.name: Sets, products of ranges and lexicographic order
known.gloss: The set [n] = {0,…,n−1}, products of such sets as multi-indices, and ordering tuples lexicographically, as in row-major storage of a multidimensional array.

known.name: Matrix transposition and row-major storage
known.gloss: The transpose swaps rows and columns of a matrix, and a matrix stored row by row on a tape must be rearranged to be read by column.

known.name: Triangle inequality and error bounds
known.gloss: Bounding the distance between computed and true values by summing errors of successive steps via |a+b| ≤ |a|+|b|, and recovering an integer from an approximation within 1/2 by rounding.

known.name: Boolean and arithmetic circuits as networks
known.gloss: A fixed finite network of gates joined by wires, each gate computing a simple function (such as XOR or a linear combination) of its input wires.

known.name: Graphs, paths and neighbors
known.gloss: Vertices joined by edges, with the notions of neighbor, path and route between two vertices.

known.name: Stacks and recursion
known.gloss: A last-in first-out structure used to implement recursive calls by saving and restoring state.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform and Karatsuba as survey knowledge
known.gloss: Multiplying polynomials or integers by evaluating at roots of unity, multiplying pointwise and interpolating, at the level of knowing the idea and its n log n flavor, without the details of the cited refinements.

known.name: Real and imaginary parts, rounding and truncation
known.gloss: Splitting a complex number into real and imaginary parts and dropping or rounding fractional bits of each.

known.name: Dot product, vectors over the rationals and orthonormal bases
known.gloss: The dot product of coordinate vectors over the rationals or reals, orthogonality, and expressing vectors in a basis.
